units.blurb_en: Why chips are stacked together, why AI needs fast memory, and how Taiwan became a chip island.
units.blurb_zh: 晶片為什麼要疊在一起、AI 為什麼需要快速的記憶體，以及台灣怎麼成為晶片島。

lessons.title: Why Do We Stack Chips Together?
lessons.title_zh: 先進封裝：為什麼要把晶片疊在一起？
lessons.blurb_en: One chip cannot be made as big as we like, so engineers put many chips into one package, side by side or stacked like floors in a building. In 3D, compare chips set apart on a board, side by side on an interposer, and stacked, then take the package apart layer by layer.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一顆晶片沒辦法想做多大就做多大，所以工程師把很多顆晶片放進同一個封裝裡：並排，或像大樓的樓層一樣疊起來。在 3D 裡比較三種放法——分開焊在板子上、並排放在中介層上、疊起來——再把封裝一層一層拆開來看。
lessons.big_idea_en: A chip needs a package to protect it and to connect it to the outside. Advanced packaging goes further: it puts several chips into one package, side by side or stacked, and joins them with very short wires. Shorter paths mean data moves faster and uses less power, like turning scattered houses into one tall building.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 晶片需要封裝來保護它，並把它和外面接起來。先進封裝更進一步：把好幾顆晶片放進同一個封裝，並排或疊起來，用很短的線連在一起。路短了，資料就跑得更快、更省電，就像把分散的房子蓋成一棟大樓。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose Apart, Side by side, or Stacked at the top left, and watch the yellow dots of data travel from the blue logic chip to the purple memory chips. Then drag “Take it apart” to pull the layers away from one another and see what a package is made of.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在左上角選「分開放」「並排」或「疊起來」，看黃色的資料小點從藍色的運算晶片跑到紫色的記憶體晶片。再拉「拆開來看」，把每一層上下拉開，看看一個封裝是用什麼做成的。

board.en: Each chip sits in its own package, and the packages are soldered to a circuit board a few centimeters apart. Data has to leave one package, cross the board, and enter another. For a chip, that is a very long trip.
board.zh: 每顆晶片各有自己的封裝，分開焊在電路板上，彼此相隔幾公分。資料要先離開一個封裝、穿過板子、再進到另一個封裝。對晶片來說，這是很遠的路。

side.en: Now the bare chips sit side by side on one thin slice of silicon called an interposer. Its wires are far finer than the ones on a circuit board, so the chips can sit very close together. This is called 2.5D packaging.
side.zh: 現在把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在同一片薄薄的矽上，這片矽叫做中介層。它上面的線比電路板上的細得多，所以晶片可以靠得非常近。這種做法叫做 2.5D 封裝。

stack.en: Here the memory chips are stacked like floors in a building. Tiny copper posts called TSVs run straight up through the chips like elevators. The data only has to go up a few floors. This is 3D packaging.
stack.zh: 這裡把記憶體晶片像大樓的樓層一樣疊起來。很細的銅柱（矽穿孔，TSV）直直穿過晶片，像電梯一樣。資料只要往上走幾層樓就到了。這就是 3D 封裝。

legend.en: Blue: the logic chip, which does the calculating
legend.zh: 藍色：運算晶片，負責計算

legend.en: Purple: memory chips, which hold the data
legend.zh: 紫色：記憶體晶片，負責放資料

legend.en: Gray-blue: the interposer, a slice of silicon with very fine wires
legend.zh: 灰藍色：中介層，一片佈滿細線的矽

legend.en: Green: the package substrate and the circuit board
legend.zh: 綠色：封裝的基板和電路板

legend.en: Yellow dots: data on its way
legend.zh: 黃色小點：正在路上的資料

lab.scale_en: A teaching diagram, not to scale. The distances (about 3 centimeters, 3 millimeters, and 0.4 millimeters) are example numbers chosen to show the pattern; real products differ. Real packages have thousands of connections where this model shows a few dozen, and real chips are much thinner than they are drawn here.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意圖，不是真實比例。距離（大約 3 公分、3 公釐、0.4 公釐）是為了呈現趨勢所舉的例子，真的產品各有不同。真的封裝有成千上萬個接點，這裡只畫了幾十個；真的晶片也比圖上薄得多。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The three layouts follow Wikipedia, “2.5D integrated circuit” and “Three-dimensional integrated circuit”. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；三種放法依維基百科「2.5D integrated circuit」與「Three-dimensional integrated circuit」條目。

paras: Look inside a phone or a computer and you will see small black squares on a green board. Those squares are not the chips themselves. Each one is a package: a tough case with a chip inside. The package protects the thin silicon from bumps, dust, and damp. It also connects the chip's tiny contacts to the much bigger world of the circuit board.

For a long time, that was the whole job. One chip went into one package, and the packages were soldered onto a board a few centimeters apart. But chips kept getting faster, and the trip between them began to matter. Data from the logic chip, which does the thinking, had to cross the board to reach the memory chip, which holds the data. Every trip took time and energy.

Why not just make one giant chip with everything on it? Because chips cannot grow without limit. The machine that prints the circuits can only expose an area of about 26 by 33 millimeters at a time. Bigger chips also mean fewer chips on each wafer, and one speck of dust can ruin a bigger piece. So engineers took a different road: keep the chips small, and bring them very close together.

The first way is to place bare chips side by side on a thin slice of silicon called an interposer. Its wires are far finer than the wires on a circuit board, so the chips can sit almost touching. This is called 2.5D packaging. Designers can mix and match small chips, called chiplets, a little like building with LEGO bricks.

The second way is to stack chips on top of one another, like floors in a building. Tiny copper posts called through-silicon vias, or TSVs, run straight through the chips like elevators. Now the data travels up a few floors instead of across a city. Shorter wires mean faster signals and less wasted power. But a stack traps heat, so engineers must plan carefully how to keep it cool.

After packaging, every chip is tested before it leaves the factory. Packaging and testing together are a big industry in Taiwan. ASE, founded in Kaohsiung in 1984, is the world's largest company that packages and tests chips for other companies. So the next time you hear about “advanced packaging,” think of a tall building: many chips, living close together, working as one.
paras_zh: 打開手機或電腦，你會看到綠色的板子上有一個個黑色的小方塊。那些方塊並不是晶片本身，而是封裝：一個堅固的外殼，晶片在裡面。封裝保護薄薄的矽不被碰撞、灰塵和濕氣傷害，也把晶片上很小的接點，接到電路板那個大得多的世界。
很長一段時間，封裝的工作就只有這些。一顆晶片放進一個封裝，一個個封裝焊在板子上，彼此相隔幾公分。可是晶片越來越快，晶片之間的那段路開始變得重要。負責思考的運算晶片送出資料，要穿過板子才到得了負責放資料的記憶體晶片。每走一趟，都要花時間和電。
那為什麼不乾脆做一顆很大的晶片，把所有東西都放在上面？因為晶片沒辦法無限制地變大。印電路的機器一次只能曝光大約 26 × 33 公釐的範圍。晶片越大，一片晶圓能做的顆數也越少，而且一粒灰塵就會毀掉更大的一塊。所以工程師走了另一條路：晶片維持小小的，但是讓它們靠得非常近。
第一種方法，是把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在一片薄薄的矽上，這片矽叫做中介層。它上面的線比電路板上的細得多，所以晶片幾乎可以貼在一起。這種做法叫做 2.5D 封裝。設計的人可以把叫做「小晶片」（chiplet）的小塊自由搭配，有點像玩樂高積木。
第二種方法，是把晶片一顆疊在另一顆上面，像大樓的樓層。叫做矽穿孔（TSV）的細銅柱直直穿過晶片，像電梯一樣。現在資料只要往上走幾層樓，不必橫越整個城市。線短了，訊號更快，浪費的電也更少。不過疊起來容易悶住熱，所以工程師要仔細規劃怎麼散熱。
封裝好之後，每一顆晶片都要經過測試才能出廠。封裝和測試合起來（簡稱封測）是台灣很大的產業。1984 年在高雄創立的日月光，是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。下次聽到「先進封裝」，就想像一棟高樓：很多顆晶片住得很近，一起工作，像一顆晶片一樣。
questions: What two jobs does a chip's package do?
Why don't engineers simply make one giant chip?
How is stacking chips like a tall building?
answers: It protects the chip from damage, and it connects the chip's tiny contacts to the circuit board.
The machine that prints circuits can only expose about 26 by 33 millimeters at a time, bigger chips mean fewer per wafer, and one speck of dust ruins a bigger piece.
The chips are like floors, and the TSVs are like elevators. Data goes up a few floors instead of traveling a long way across a board.

vocab.exzh: 把書整齊地疊在桌上。

vocab.exzh: 我家到學校的距離是兩公里。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Three packages, each with one chip. Follow the yellow dots along the gold lines: it is a long way from the logic chip to the memory.
parts.text_zh: 三個封裝，各裝一顆晶片。跟著黃色小點沿著金色的線走：從運算晶片到記憶體要走很遠。

parts.text_en: One package, five chips. They sit on an interposer, so close that the trip is ten times shorter in this model.
parts.text_zh: 一個封裝，五顆晶片。它們放在中介層上，靠得很近，在這個模型裡路程短了十倍。

parts.text_en: The memory chips become two towers, eight floors each. The gold posts are the elevators.
parts.text_zh: 記憶體晶片變成兩座塔，各有八層樓。金色的柱子就是電梯。

parts.text_en: From the bottom: circuit board, solder balls, substrate, tiny bumps, interposer, and the chips on top.
parts.text_zh: 從最下面開始：電路板、錫球、基板、細小的凸塊、中介層，最上面才是晶片。

lessons.parts_note_en: The distances in the panel are examples, but the pattern is real: each step brings the chips closer together.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 面板上的距離是舉例，但趨勢是真的：每換一種放法，晶片就靠得更近。

links_head.en: Where the chips come from, and where the limit comes from
links_head.zh: 晶片從哪裡來，那個上限又是怎麼來的

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體 第四課
links.en: How Do You Draw a Circuit Smaller Than a Virus?
links.zh: 怎麼畫出比病毒還小的電路？
links.note_en: Why one exposure is at most 26 × 33 millimeters.
links.note_zh: 為什麼一次曝光最大只有 26 × 33 公釐。

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體 第三課
links.en: How Does Sand Become a Chip?
links.note_en: Why bigger chips mean fewer chips on each wafer.
links.note_zh: 為什麼晶片越大，一片晶圓做得出來的顆數越少。

pack.eyebrow: Build a Package · 組一個封裝
pack.en: How many chips are in one package?
pack.zh: 一個封裝裡有幾顆晶片？
pack.lead_en: Put logic chips in the middle, add stacks of memory around them, and choose how many chips are in each stack. Count how many chips end up working as one.
pack.lead_zh: 把運算晶片放在中間，旁邊加上幾疊記憶體，再選每一疊有幾層。數數看，最後有幾顆晶片像一顆晶片一樣一起工作。
pack.note_en: This is a toy layout, not a real product. Stacks of 16 or more chips have been built. A single chip, by comparison, can be at most about 26 × 33 millimeters, the area of one exposure.
pack.note_zh: 這是示意的排法，不是哪一個真的產品。現實中已經有疊到 16 層以上的晶片。相比之下，單一顆晶片最大只能大約 26 × 33 公釐，也就是一次曝光的範圍。

facts.eyebrow: Packaging by the Numbers · 封裝的數字
facts.lead_en: Five numbers and names behind advanced packaging.
facts.lead_zh: 先進封裝背後的五個數字和名字。

items.en: The largest area one exposure can print. A single chip cannot be bigger than this.
items.zh: 一次曝光能印的最大範圍。單一顆晶片不能比這更大。

items.en: Bare chips placed next to one another on a silicon interposer, inside one package.
items.zh: 把沒有外殼的晶片並排放在矽中介層上，裝在同一個封裝裡。

items.en: Three-dimensional chips have been made by stacking as many as 16 or more chips.
items.zh: 3D 晶片已經做到把 16 顆以上的晶片疊在一起。

items.en: IBM began turning chips upside down and joining them with tiny balls of solder instead of wires.
items.zh: IBM 開始把晶片翻過來，用小小的錫球取代金屬線來連接。

items.en: ASE opened its first factory. It is now the world's largest packaging and testing company for other firms.
items.zh: 日月光的第一座工廠啟用。現在它是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。

culture_cards.title_en: An upside-down chip, LEGO bricks, a harbor city, and a long name
culture_cards.title_zh: 一顆翻過來的晶片、樂高積木、一座港都、一個很長的名字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four stories about putting chips together.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於「把晶片放在一起」的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Early chips were joined to their packages by thin wires around the edges. In the 1960s IBM tried something different for its big computers: put tiny balls of solder on the chip, flip the chip face down, and melt the balls onto the package. This is called a flip chip. It allows many more connections, because the whole face of the chip can be used.
cards.body_zh: 早期的晶片是用邊緣一圈細細的金屬線接到封裝上。1960 年代，IBM 為了它的大型電腦試了不一樣的做法：在晶片上放小小的錫球，把晶片正面朝下翻過來，再把錫球熔接到封裝上。這叫做覆晶。這樣能做出多很多的接點，因為晶片的整個面都可以用。

cards.body_en: Instead of one big chip that does everything, designers can make several small chips, each good at one job, and place them side by side on an interposer. These small chips are called chiplets. People often compare them to LEGO bricks, because they can be mixed and matched.
cards.body_zh: 與其做一顆什麼都包的大晶片，設計的人可以做幾顆小晶片，每一顆專門做一件事，再把它們並排放在中介層上。這些小晶片叫做 chiplet。大家常把它們比做樂高積木，因為可以自由搭配。

cards.body_en: ASE was founded in 1984 by two brothers, who opened its first factory in Kaohsiung. Today its headquarters and main operations are still there, and it is the world's largest company that packages and tests chips for others. A chip designed in one country and made in Hsinchu or Tainan may well be packaged in Kaohsiung.
cards.body_zh: 日月光在 1984 年由一對兄弟創立，第一座工廠就在高雄。今天它的總部和主要的工廠還是在那裡，也是全世界最大的封裝測試代工公司。一顆在別的國家設計、在新竹或台南製造的晶片，很可能是在高雄封裝的。

cards.zh: 晶片放在晶圓上、再放在基板上
cards.body_en: You may see the word CoWoS in the news. It is TSMC's name for one kind of 2.5D packaging, and it simply describes the layers from top to bottom: Chip on Wafer on Substrate. The “wafer” in the middle is the silicon interposer.
cards.body_zh: 新聞裡常看到 CoWoS 這個字。它是台積電替一種 2.5D 封裝取的名字，意思就是從上到下的三層：晶片（Chip）放在晶圓（Wafer）上，再放在基板（Substrate）上。中間的那片「晶圓」就是矽中介層。

myths.myth_en: The black square on the circuit board is the chip.
myths.myth_zh: 電路板上的黑色方塊就是晶片。
myths.fact_en: It is the package. The chip is a thin piece of silicon sealed inside it.
myths.fact_zh: 那是封裝。晶片是封在裡面的一片薄薄的矽。

myths.myth_en: Packaging is just a box. It does not matter how it is done.
myths.myth_zh: 封裝只是一個盒子，怎麼做都沒差。
myths.fact_en: The package decides how close chips can be and how many connections they have, so it affects speed and power.
myths.fact_zh: 封裝決定晶片能靠多近、能有多少接點，所以會影響速度和耗電。

myths.myth_en: If we want more power, we can simply make one chip bigger and bigger.
myths.myth_zh: 想要更強，把一顆晶片越做越大就好了。
myths.fact_en: One exposure covers at most about 26 × 33 millimeters, and bigger chips mean fewer good chips from each wafer.
myths.fact_zh: 一次曝光最大只有大約 26 × 33 公釐；晶片越大，每片晶圓做得出來的好晶片也越少。

myths.myth_en: Stacking is always better than placing chips side by side.
myths.myth_zh: 疊起來一定比並排好。
myths.fact_en: Stacking makes the paths shortest, but it traps heat. Placing chips side by side keeps them cooler. Engineers choose what fits the job.
myths.fact_zh: 疊起來路最短，但容易悶住熱；並排比較好散熱。工程師會看用途來選。

tricks.body_en: It guards the chip and links it to the board.
tricks.body_zh: 保護晶片，並把它接到電路板上。

tricks.body_en: Apart on a board, side by side (2.5D), stacked (3D).
tricks.body_zh: 分開放在板子上、並排（2.5D）、疊起來（3D）。

tricks.body_en: They carry signals straight up through the chips.
tricks.body_zh: 它們帶著訊號直直往上穿過晶片。

tricks.body_en: But a tall stack needs a way to lose its heat.
tricks.body_zh: 不過疊得高，就要想辦法把熱散掉。

safety.en: Do not open phones, computers, or chargers to look for chips. They can hold a dangerous charge, and the parts are sharp.
safety.zh: 不要為了找晶片去拆手機、電腦或充電器。裡面可能還帶著危險的電，零件也很銳利。

safety.en: Old circuit boards from a recycling bin may have sharp edges. Ask an adult to check them first, and wash your hands afterward.
safety.zh: 回收來的舊電路板邊緣可能很利。先請大人檢查過，摸完要洗手。

safety.en: Small bricks and beads are a choking danger. Keep them away from little children.
safety.zh: 小積木和珠子可能噎到小小孩，不要讓他們拿到。

safety.en: Pick up string and bricks from the floor when you finish so that nobody trips.
safety.zh: 活動結束後，把地上的繩子和積木收好，免得有人絆倒。

materials.en: Building bricks in two colors (one color for logic, one for memory) and a large baseplate or a sheet of cardboard
materials.zh: 兩種顏色的積木（一種當運算晶片，一種當記憶體），和一塊大底板或厚紙板

materials.en: String, scissors, and a ruler
materials.zh: 繩子、剪刀和尺

steps.en: City 1: put one logic brick and four memory bricks far apart on the board. Use string to connect the logic brick to each memory brick.
steps.zh: 第一座城市：把一塊運算積木和四塊記憶體積木分開放在底板上，用繩子把運算積木和每一塊記憶體積木連起來。

steps.en: City 2: place the same five bricks side by side on a small plate. Connect them with string again.
steps.zh: 第二座城市：把同樣五塊積木並排放在一塊小板子上，再用繩子連一次。

steps.en: City 3: stack the four memory bricks into a tower beside the logic brick, and connect them.
steps.zh: 第三座城市：把四塊記憶體積木疊成一座塔，放在運算積木旁邊，再連起來。

steps.en: Measure all the string you used for each city. Which city needs the least?
steps.zh: 量一量每座城市用掉的繩子總長。哪一座用得最少？

activities.tip_en: The string is the wire. Less string means a shorter trip for the data, and less energy spent on the way.
activities.tip_zh: 繩子就是電線。繩子越短，資料走的路越短，路上花的電也越少。

materials.en: Ten small cards with numbers on them, and a timer
materials.zh: 十張寫著數字的小卡片，和一個計時器

materials.en: A classroom with space to move
materials.zh: 一間可以走動的教室

steps.en: One student is the logic chip, and another is the memory. First they stand at opposite ends of the classroom.
steps.zh: 一位同學當運算晶片，另一位當記憶體。先讓他們站在教室的兩頭。

steps.en: The logic chip carries the ten cards to the memory one at a time. Time how long it takes.
steps.zh: 運算晶片把十張卡片一張一張送到記憶體那裡。計時看要花多久。

steps.en: Now they stand side by side and do it again. Then try it with the memory sitting right in front of the logic chip.
steps.zh: 現在讓他們並排站，再做一次。接著讓記憶體就坐在運算晶片的正前方，再試一次。

steps.en: Compare the three times. Who got tired? What does that tell you about power?
steps.zh: 比較三次的時間。誰累了？這和「耗電」有什麼關係？

activities.tip_en: Walk, do not run. The point is the distance, not the speed of the runner.
activities.tip_zh: 用走的，不要跑。重點是距離，不是跑的人有多快。

sources.en: Packaging is the final stage of making a chip: the die is put in a case that prevents damage and corrosion and connects it to the circuit board; packaging is followed by testing
sources.zh: 封裝是製造晶片的最後階段：把晶粒放進能防止損傷與腐蝕的外殼，並連接到電路板；封裝之後進行測試

sources.en: 2.5D: several dies side by side on a silicon interposer in one package; placing dies side by side reduces heat buildup; chiplets combined LEGO-style; TSMC's CoWoS (Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate)
sources.zh: 2.5D：多顆晶粒並排放在矽中介層上、裝在同一個封裝；並排可減少積熱；小晶片像樂高一樣組合；台積電的 CoWoS

sources.en: 3D: stacking as many as 16 or more chips, connected vertically with through-silicon vias; shorter wires, less power
sources.zh: 3D：把 16 顆以上的晶片疊起來，用矽穿孔上下連接；線更短、更省電

sources.en: A through-silicon via is a vertical electrical connection that passes completely through a silicon wafer or die
sources.zh: 矽穿孔是完全穿過矽晶圓或晶粒的垂直電氣連接

sources.en: An interposer spreads or reroutes connections; it can be made of silicon or organic material
sources.zh: 中介層用來把接點展開或重新佈線；可以用矽或有機材料製作

sources.en: Flip chip: solder bumps on the chip, which is flipped face down; introduced commercially by IBM in the 1960s
sources.zh: 覆晶：在晶片上做錫球凸塊，再把晶片正面朝下翻過來；1960 年代由 IBM 商業化

sources.en: The EUV exposure field is 26 × 33 mm
sources.zh: EUV 一次曝光的範圍是 26 × 33 公釐

sources.en: ASE: founded in 1984 with its first factory in Kaohsiung; headquarters in Kaohsiung; the largest outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) provider according to Gartner
sources.zh: 日月光：1984 年創立，第一座工廠在高雄；總部在高雄；依 Gartner 是最大的封裝測試代工（OSAT）業者

lessons.title: What Is HBM, and Why Does AI Need It?
lessons.title_zh: HBM 是什麼？AI 為什麼需要它？
lessons.blurb_en: An AI chip can calculate very fast, but it often has to wait for its data. HBM is memory stacked like a tower right beside the chip and joined to it by a road with more than a thousand lanes. In 3D, compare ordinary memory with four generations of HBM, then work out how many movies it could move in one second.
lessons.blurb_zh: AI 晶片算得很快，卻常常要等資料。HBM 是像高塔一樣疊起來的記憶體，就放在晶片旁邊，中間是一條有上千個車道的路。在 3D 裡比較一般記憶體和四代 HBM，再算算它一秒可以搬幾部電影。
lessons.big_idea_en: A fast chip is no use if its data arrives slowly. HBM, short for High Bandwidth Memory, stacks memory chips into a tower, connects the floors with tiny elevators called TSVs, and sets the tower right next to the logic chip. More than a thousand data lines join them, like a very wide, very short highway, so huge amounts of data move at once.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 資料送得慢，晶片再快也沒用。HBM 是「高頻寬記憶體」（High Bandwidth Memory）的縮寫：把記憶體晶片疊成一座塔，用叫做矽穿孔的小電梯連接每一層，再把塔緊貼著運算晶片放。上千條資料線把兩邊連起來，像一條又寬又短的高速公路，一次就能送很多資料。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Start with “Ordinary memory”: the memory chips are far across the board, and the road has few lanes. Then choose HBM. The memory becomes a tower beside the blue logic chip, and the road becomes short and wide. Pick a generation on the right to see the lanes, the floors, and the speed change.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。先看「一般記憶體」：記憶體晶片在板子的另一頭，路上沒幾個車道。再選 HBM：記憶體變成藍色運算晶片旁邊的一座塔，路變得又短又寬。在右邊選世代，看車道、樓層和速度怎麼變。

far.en: Ordinary memory sits in its own packages, some distance from the logic chip. Each memory chip has only a few dozen data lines, and the trip is long. The logic chip finishes its work and waits.
far.zh: 一般的記憶體各有自己的封裝，離運算晶片有一段距離。每顆記憶體晶片只有幾十條資料線，路又長。運算晶片算完了，只能等。

hbm1.en: The first HBM became a standard in 2013. Four memory chips are stacked, and 1,024 data lines join the stack to the logic chip. That is 32 times as many as an ordinary graphics memory chip has.
hbm1.zh: 第一代 HBM 在 2013 年成為標準。四層記憶體疊在一起，用 1,024 條資料線接到運算晶片，是一顆一般顯示卡記憶體的 32 倍。

hbm2.en: HBM2 arrived in 2016. The road is still 1,024 lanes wide, but each lane carries data more than twice as fast, and the tower can be eight floors tall.
hbm2.zh: HBM2 在 2016 年推出。路還是 1,024 個車道，但每個車道送資料的速度快了兩倍多，塔也可以疊到八層。

hbm3.en: HBM3 came in 2022. Each lane is faster again, and one stack can move about 819 gigabytes every second.
hbm3.zh: HBM3 在 2022 年推出。每個車道又更快了，一疊每秒能送大約 819 GB。

hbm4.en: HBM4, set as a standard in 2025, doubles the road to 2,048 lanes, and the tower can have 16 floors. One stack can move about 2,048 gigabytes every second.
hbm4.zh: 2025 年訂出標準的 HBM4，把路加寬一倍到 2,048 個車道，塔也可以疊到 16 層。一疊每秒能送大約 2,048 GB。

legend.en: Blue: the logic chip, which does the calculating
legend.zh: 藍色：運算晶片，負責計算

legend.en: Purple: memory chips (stacked, in HBM)
legend.zh: 紫色：記憶體晶片（HBM 是疊起來的）

legend.en: Gray road with lane lines: the data lines. One lane in the model stands for 64 real data lines
legend.zh: 有車道線的灰色路面：資料線。模型裡的一個車道代表 64 條真的資料線

legend.en: Small cars: data on the move (yellow going one way, blue the other)
legend.zh: 小車子：正在移動的資料（黃色往一邊、藍色往另一邊）

lab.scale_en: A teaching diagram, not to scale. The numbers of data lines, floors, and gigabytes per second come from the published HBM standards. The road, the cars, and the distances are only pictures: real data lines are thin wires inside the interposer, and data is electrical signals, not cars. The ordinary memory shown is graphics memory, whose chips each have 32 data lines; it is drawn with a single lane.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意圖，不是真實比例。資料線數、樓層數和每秒幾 GB 來自公開的 HBM 標準。路、車子和距離都只是比喻：真的資料線是中介層裡的細線，資料是電的訊號，不是車子。圖裡的一般記憶體是顯示卡記憶體，每顆晶片 32 條資料線，模型裡畫成一個車道。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The figures for each generation follow the table in Wikipedia, “High Bandwidth Memory”, which cites the JEDEC standards. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；各代的數字依維基百科「High Bandwidth Memory」條目的規格表（引自 JEDEC 標準）。

paras: Imagine the best cook in the world working in a kitchen where the refrigerator is at the other end of the street. The cook is fast, but most of the time is spent walking to fetch the eggs. A chip that runs AI has the same trouble. It can do an enormous number of calculations each second, but only if the numbers it needs arrive in time.

Those numbers are kept in memory chips. In an ordinary computer, the memory sits in its own packages some distance from the logic chip, and each memory chip talks through only a few dozen data lines. For everyday work that is fine. For AI, which moves mountains of data, the logic chip ends up waiting. The memory cannot deliver fast enough.

HBM was made to fix this. The letters stand for High Bandwidth Memory. Bandwidth means how much data can move in one second. Engineers did three things. First, they stacked memory chips on top of one another, like the floors of a tower. Second, they ran tiny copper posts, called TSVs, straight through the stack, like elevators, so every floor is connected.

Third, they moved the tower right next to the logic chip, on the same interposer you met in the last lesson. Because the two are so close, they can be joined by a huge number of very short wires. The first HBM had 1,024 data lines for each stack. Think of a highway with more than a thousand lanes that is very, very short.

HBM became an industry standard in 2013, and it has grown quickly since. Each new generation sends data faster through every lane, and the towers get taller: 4 floors, then 8, 12, and 16. The newest standard, HBM4, doubles the highway to 2,048 lanes. One HBM4 stack can move about 2,048 gigabytes in a single second.

That is why you now hear about HBM in the news. An AI chip usually has several HBM towers standing around it, feeding it data all day. The memory is no longer far down the street. The refrigerator has moved right beside the cook, and it has a thousand doors.
paras_zh: 想像全世界最厲害的廚師，在一間廚房裡工作，可是冰箱在街的另一頭。廚師手腳很快，但大部分的時間都花在走路去拿雞蛋。跑 AI 的晶片也有一樣的麻煩：它每秒能做非常非常多次計算，但前提是它需要的數字要及時送到。
這些數字放在記憶體晶片裡。一般的電腦，記憶體各有自己的封裝，和運算晶片隔著一段距離，而且每顆記憶體晶片只透過幾十條資料線來溝通。平常的工作這樣就夠了。可是 AI 要搬動像山一樣多的資料，運算晶片最後只能乾等，因為記憶體送得不夠快。
HBM 就是為了解決這件事做出來的。這三個字母是 High Bandwidth Memory，高頻寬記憶體；「頻寬」的意思是一秒鐘能送多少資料。工程師做了三件事。第一，把記憶體晶片一顆顆疊起來，像一座塔的樓層。第二，用叫做矽穿孔（TSV）的細銅柱直直穿過整疊晶片，像電梯一樣，讓每一層都連得到。
第三，把這座塔搬到運算晶片的正旁邊，放在上一課認識的中介層上。因為兩邊靠得這麼近，就可以用非常多條很短的線把它們連起來。第一代 HBM 每一疊就有 1,024 條資料線。想像一條有一千多個車道、卻非常非常短的高速公路。
HBM 在 2013 年成為業界標準，之後進步得很快。每一代，每個車道送資料的速度都更快，塔也越疊越高：4 層、8 層、12 層、16 層。最新的標準 HBM4，把高速公路加寬一倍到 2,048 個車道。一疊 HBM4 一秒鐘大約能送 2,048 GB 的資料。
所以現在新聞裡常聽到 HBM。一顆 AI 晶片的旁邊通常站著好幾座 HBM 的塔，整天不停地餵資料給它。記憶體不再遠在街的另一頭了：冰箱已經搬到廚師身邊，而且有一千個門。

band.en: How many movies in one second?
band.lead_en: Suppose one movie file is 5 gigabytes. Choose a generation of HBM and how many stacks stand beside the chip, and see how many movies' worth of data they could move every second.
band.lead_zh: 假設一部電影的檔案是 5 GB。選一代 HBM、選晶片旁邊放幾疊，看看它們每秒可以搬動相當於幾部電影的資料。
band.note_en: The 5-gigabyte movie and the home internet speeds are examples. The gigabytes per second for each generation are the top figures in the standards for one stack; real products may run below them.
band.note_zh: 5 GB 的電影和家用網路的速度都是舉例。各代每秒幾 GB 是標準裡一疊的最高數字，實際的產品可能比較低。

facts.eyebrow: HBM by the Numbers · HBM 的數字
facts.lead_en: Six numbers from the HBM standards.
facts.lead_zh: HBM 標準裡的六個數字。

items.en: HBM was adopted as an industry standard in October 2013.
items.zh: HBM 在 2013 年 10 月成為業界標準。

items.en: The width of the road for one stack in the first three generations.
items.zh: 前三代，每一疊的「路寬」。

items.en: An ordinary graphics memory chip has 32 data lines. An HBM stack has 32 times as many.
items.zh: 一顆一般的顯示卡記憶體有 32 條資料線，一疊 HBM 是它的 32 倍。

items.en: The tallest stack in the newest standards: sixteen memory chips, one on top of another.
items.zh: 最新標準裡最高的一疊：十六顆記憶體晶片一顆疊一顆。

items.en: The 2025 standard doubles the road.
items.zh: 2025 年的標準把路加寬一倍。

items.en: From 128 gigabytes a second in 2013 to 2,048 in 2025, for a single stack.
items.zh: 單一疊的速度，從 2013 年的每秒 128 GB 到 2025 年的 2,048 GB。

culture_cards.title_en: A word, a committee, a tower, and three makers
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個詞、一個委員會、一座塔、三家公司
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories behind three letters.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 三個字母背後的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Bandwidth tells you how much data can pass in one second. You can raise it in two ways: add more lanes, or make each lane faster. HBM does both. That is why it has “High Bandwidth” in its name.
cards.body_zh: 頻寬告訴你一秒鐘能通過多少資料。要提高它有兩個辦法：增加車道，或讓每個車道更快。HBM 兩樣都做，所以名字裡才有「高頻寬」。

cards.body_en: HBM was first developed by Samsung, AMD, and SK Hynix, and in October 2013 an industry group called JEDEC adopted it as a standard. A standard means that memory from different makers fits the same chips, the way any plug fits a socket made to the same standard.
cards.body_zh: HBM 最早是三星、超微（AMD）和 SK 海力士開發的；2013 年 10 月，叫做 JEDEC 的產業組織把它訂成標準。有了標準，不同公司做的記憶體就能配同樣的晶片，就像照同一個標準做的插頭都插得進插座。

cards.body_en: The first HBM stacks had four memory chips. Later generations went to eight, then twelve, then sixteen. As the tower grows, each chip has to be thinner, and the tiny posts that run through them must line up from floor to floor.
cards.body_zh: 第一代 HBM 疊四顆記憶體晶片，後來變成八顆、十二顆、十六顆。塔越高，每一顆晶片就要越薄，穿過它們的細柱也要一層一層對得剛剛好。

cards.body_en: In 2025 the world's largest makers of HBM were SK Hynix and Samsung of South Korea and Micron of the United States. The towers are then joined to logic chips by advanced packaging, the subject of the last lesson.
cards.body_zh: 2025 年全世界最大的 HBM 製造商，是南韓的 SK 海力士和三星，以及美國的美光。這些塔接著要靠先進封裝（上一課的主題）和運算晶片接在一起。

myths.myth_en: HBM is a kind of AI chip that does the thinking.
myths.myth_zh: HBM 是一種負責思考的 AI 晶片。
myths.fact_en: HBM is memory. It holds the data and hands it over quickly. The calculating is done by the logic chip beside it.
myths.fact_zh: HBM 是記憶體，負責放資料、並且很快地交出去。計算是旁邊的運算晶片做的。

myths.myth_en: High bandwidth just means the memory holds more.
myths.myth_zh: 高頻寬就是記憶體裝得比較多。
myths.fact_en: Bandwidth is about speed of delivery: how much data moves each second. How much the memory holds is called capacity.
myths.fact_zh: 頻寬講的是送得多快：每秒搬多少資料。能裝多少叫做容量。

myths.myth_en: A faster logic chip always makes the whole computer faster.
myths.myth_zh: 運算晶片越快，整台電腦就一定越快。
myths.fact_en: Not if it has to wait for data. A fast cook with a faraway refrigerator is still slow.
myths.fact_zh: 如果它要等資料，就不一定。冰箱在很遠的地方，再快的廚師也快不起來。

myths.myth_en: HBM is just ordinary memory with a new name.
myths.myth_zh: HBM 只是一般記憶體換個名字。
myths.fact_en: It is built differently: chips stacked with TSVs, set beside the logic chip, and joined by over a thousand data lines.
myths.fact_zh: 它的做法不一樣：用矽穿孔把晶片疊起來、放在運算晶片旁邊、用上千條資料線相連。

tricks.body_en: HBM is memory moved right next to the chip.
tricks.body_zh: HBM 就是搬到晶片旁邊的記憶體。

tricks.body_en: Memory chips are stacked, and TSVs connect the floors.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體晶片疊起來，矽穿孔連接每一層。

tricks.body_en: 1,024 data lines in each stack, and 2,048 in HBM4.
tricks.body_zh: 每一疊 1,024 條資料線，HBM4 是 2,048 條。

tricks.body_en: That is what bandwidth means.
tricks.body_zh: 這就是頻寬的意思。

safety.en: Do not open computers, graphics cards, or servers to look for memory. They can be damaged by a tiny spark from your fingers, and some parts stay charged.
safety.zh: 不要為了找記憶體去拆電腦、顯示卡或伺服器。手指上一點點靜電就可能弄壞零件，有些零件還帶著電。

safety.en: In the highway game, walk. Mark the lanes clearly so that nobody bumps into anyone else.
safety.zh: 玩高速公路遊戲的時候用走的。把車道標清楚，免得互相撞到。

safety.en: Keep small cards and tokens away from little children.
safety.zh: 小卡片和代幣不要讓小小孩拿到。

materials.en: Forty small cards (the data), a timer, and tape to mark lanes on the floor
materials.zh: 四十張小卡片（資料）、計時器，和在地上貼車道用的膠帶

materials.en: Two tables: one is the memory, one is the logic chip
materials.zh: 兩張桌子：一張當記憶體，一張當運算晶片

steps.en: Round 1: put the tables far apart with one lane between them. One student at a time carries one card. How many cards arrive in one minute?
steps.zh: 第一回合：兩張桌子離很遠，中間只有一個車道。一次只能一位同學拿一張卡片走過去。一分鐘送到幾張？

steps.en: Round 2: keep the distance, but mark four lanes. Four students can walk at once.
steps.zh: 第二回合：距離不變，但是貼出四個車道，可以四位同學同時走。

steps.en: Round 3: push the tables close together and keep the four lanes.
steps.zh: 第三回合：把兩張桌子推近，維持四個車道。

steps.en: Write down the cards per minute for each round. That number is the bandwidth. Which change helped more: more lanes, or a shorter road?
steps.zh: 記下每一回合每分鐘送到幾張，這個數字就是頻寬。哪一種改變幫助比較大：車道變多，還是路變短？

activities.tip_en: HBM does both at once: far more lanes, and a much shorter road.
activities.tip_zh: HBM 兩樣一起做：車道多很多，路也短很多。

materials.en: Sixteen squares of cardboard, all the same size
materials.zh: 十六片一樣大的方形厚紙板

materials.en: Drinking straws, a hole punch, and a marker
materials.zh: 吸管、打洞器和麥克筆

steps.en: Punch four holes in the same places on every square. These are the TSVs.
steps.zh: 在每一片紙板的同樣位置打四個洞，這些就是矽穿孔。

steps.en: Write a different number on each square. These are the data.
steps.zh: 在每一片上寫一個不同的數字，這些就是資料。

steps.en: Thread the straws through the holes to stack four squares, then eight, then sixteen.
steps.zh: 把吸管穿過洞，先疊四片，再疊八片，最後疊十六片。

steps.en: What gets harder as the tower grows? What would happen if one hole were in the wrong place?
steps.zh: 塔越高，什麼事變得越難？如果有一個洞打歪了，會怎麼樣？

activities.tip_en: In a real stack, a great many posts must line up through every chip. That is one reason tall stacks are hard to make.
activities.tip_zh: 真的堆疊裡，非常多根細柱要穿過每一顆晶片、全部對準。這是高的堆疊很難做的原因之一。

sources.en: HBM: an interface for 3D-stacked memory, first developed by Samsung, AMD, and SK Hynix; adopted by JEDEC as an industry standard in October 2013; HBM2 in January 2016
sources.zh: HBM：3D 堆疊記憶體的介面，最早由三星、超微與 SK 海力士開發；2013 年 10 月由 JEDEC 訂為業界標準；HBM2 於 2016 年 1 月

sources.en: Specification table: HBM (2013) 1,024 bits, 4 dies, 128 GB/s; HBM2 (2016) 8 dies, 307 GB/s; HBM3 (2022) 12 dies, 819 GB/s; HBM4 (April 2025) 2,048 bits, 16 dies, 2,048 GB/s per stack
The HBM bus is very wide: 1,024 bits for a stack, compared with 32 bits for a GDDR memory chip; an interposer connects the memory and the processor and keeps them physically close
sources.zh: HBM 的匯流排很寬：一疊 1,024 位元，GDDR 記憶體每顆 32 位元；用中介層連接記憶體與處理器，讓兩者靠得很近

sources.en: In 2025 the largest makers of HBM included SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron Technology; demand has risen sharply because of AI
sources.zh: 2025 年最大的 HBM 製造商包括 SK 海力士、三星電子與美光；因為 AI，需求大幅上升

sources.en: A through-silicon via is a vertical electrical connection that passes completely through a silicon die
sources.zh: 矽穿孔是完全穿過矽晶粒的垂直電氣連接
